title: Magnetic Field-Tunable Repulsive Exciton-Exciton Interaction in the van der Waals Antiferromagnet NiPS$_3$
authors: Kaiyang Huang, Jaena Park, Zhuo Yang, Je-Geun Park, Atsuhiko Miyata, Yoshimitsu Kohama, Yasuhiro H. Matsuda
abstract: Two ultra-narrow absorption peaks around 1.5 eV, which are widely believed to originate from a transition from a spin-orbital entangled triplet to a singlet state, in the two-dimensional van der Waals crystal NiPS$_3$, have attracted considerable attention because of their pronounced spin-dependent character. An interesting question is whether ultrahigh magnetic fields modify an interaction-driven hybridization between those two peaks. In this work we perform systematic magneto-optical measurements of NiPS$_3$ in pulsed magnetic fields of up to 178 T and observe a pronounced mutual repulsion between the two sharp exciton peaks accompanied by a redistribution of oscillator strength, while the band edge shows no detectable field-induced shift within our experimental resolution. We construct a minimal two-level interaction model and compare it semi-quantitatively with the experimental data. Our results reveal a magnetic-field-tunable exciton-exciton coupling as the dominant high-field response of NiPS$_3$, and clarify this material as a new experimental platform for exploring strongly correlated exciton physics in magnetic van der Waals insulators.
summary: This work uses high-field magneto-optics to study the excitons in the antiferromagnet NiPS3. The researchers found that the two excitonic peaks repel each other in energy as the magnetic field increases, demonstrating a strong, tunable exciton-exciton coupling. This establishes NiPS3 as a novel material platform for exploring correlated exciton physics.
main_problem: The study investigates how ultrahigh magnetic fields modify the interaction-driven hybridization between two sharp excitonic peaks in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS3.
main_result: The research reveals a pronounced, magnetic-field-tunable exciton-exciton coupling as the dominant high-field response, confirmed by systematic magneto-optical measurements.
method: Systematic magneto-optical measurements were performed using pulsed magnetic fields up to 178 T, complemented by fitting the data to a minimal two-level interaction model.
model_or_system: The physical system is the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS3, which is modeled using a minimal two-level Hamiltonian describing coupled excitons whose interaction is tunable by the external magnetic field.
key_observables: Energy shifts of the two exciton peaks (opposite shifts observed), redistribution of oscillator strength, and the field dependence of these shifts.
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength (up to 178 T), temperature (down to 1.4 K), and the antiferromagnetic ordering temperature (Néel temperature).
main_assumptions: The system can be accurately described by a minimal two-level interaction model, and the observed shifts are dominated by exciton-exciton coupling rather than simple diamagnetic effects.
figures_summary: Figures show the field dependence of exciton peak energies up to 178 T, illustrating the repulsion and energy splitting, alongside temperature and field angle dependence of these shifts.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and the initial problem, presents the high-field magneto-optical measurements, models the interaction using a two-level Hamiltonian, and concludes by quantifying the field-tunable exciton coupling.
why_interesting: The observation of tunable exciton interactions in a solid-state magnetic insulator provides a clean, controllable platform to study strongly correlated many-body physics, analogous to cavity QED systems but realized in condensed matter.
